status.en: 243 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, most of them in Kyiv, Moscow and Odesa.
status.nb: 243 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, flest i Kyiv, Moscow og Odesa.

summary.en: In the past week 243 armed incidents were reported, many in Kyiv, Moscow and Odesa, and 62 of them were carried by two or more outlets. The UCDP recorded 75 767 battle‑related deaths in 2024. Recent strikes have hit civilian infrastructure, including a diesel deal dispute, drone attacks on Yandex data centres in Russia and a missile warhead recovered in Kyiv. Ukraine is also stepping up strikes on Russian tech infrastructure, while Russian forces continue attacks on settlements in Kharkiv region and high‑rise buildings in Dnipro.
summary.nb: I løpet av den siste uken ble 243 væpnede hendelser rapportert, mange i Kyiv, Moskva og Odesa, og 62 av dem ble dekket av to eller flere kilder. UCDP registrerte 75 767 kamprelaterte dødsfall i 2024. Nylige angrep har truffet sivil infrastruktur, inkludert en dieselavtale‑konflikt, droner som rammet Yandex‑datasentre i Russland og en missilkrone funnet i Kyiv. Ukraina intensiverer også angrep på russisk teknologiinfrastruktur, mens russiske styrker fortsetter angrep på bosetninger i Kharkiv‑regionen og høye bygninger i Dnipro.

background.title: Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)
background.extract: On 24 February 2022, Russia invaded Ukraine, starting the largest and deadliest war in Europe since World War II, in a major escalation of the existing war between the two countries that began when Russia attacked Ukraine in 2014. The fighting has caused hundreds of thousands of military casualties and tens of thousands of Ukrainian civilian casualties. Russian troops occupy roughly 20% of Ukraine. From a population of 41 million, about 8 million Ukrainians have been internally displaced and 6–7 million have fled the country, creating Europe's largest refugee crisis since World War II.
